statement: The function returns a result r, and r is true if and only if for every integer x with left <= x <= right, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(ranges) such that start_i <= x <= end_i. Here start_i and end_i are the two entries of ranges[i], and intervals are inclusive.
preconditions: Write len(ranges) for the number of intervals and, for each index i with 0 <= i < len(ranges), write ranges[i] = [start_i, end_i]. Preconditions: 1 <= len(ranges) <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < len(ranges), ranges[i] has length exactly 2 and 1 <= start_i <= end_i <= 50; and 1 <= left <= right <= 50.

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail: it does not return an error, panic, or out-of-bounds/overflow failure for any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Write len(ranges) for the number of intervals and, for each index i with 0 <= i < len(ranges), write ranges[i] = [start_i, end_i]. Preconditions: 1 <= len(ranges) <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < len(ranges), ranges[i] has length exactly 2 and 1 <= start_i <= end_i <= 50; and 1 <= left <= right <= 50.

statement: Whenever the function returns false, there exists an integer x with left <= x <= right such that for every index i with 0 <= i < len(ranges), either x < start_i or x > end_i. In other words, a false answer always has a witness x in [left, right] that is not covered by any interval.

statement: If there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(ranges) such that start_i <= left and right <= end_i, then the function returns true.
